models_n: 10 VLMs: 8 open-source (BLIP-2, InstructBLIP, mPLUG-Owl2, LLaVA-1.5, InternVL-1.5 2B and 26B, InternLM-XC2 1.8B and 7B) and 2 proprietary (Gemini, GPT-4V)
headline: LLaVA-1.5 baseline sycophancy rate of 94.6% on MM-SY
headline_loc: Section 3.3.2 (Main Results), Table 2; consistent with Table 1, where LLaVA-1.5 averages 99.4/94.6/89.7 across the three tones. Abstract gives no numbers.
quote: Firstly, the LLaVA baseline exhibits a serious sycophancy problem (94.6 Syc).
notes: Read v1 PDF (Oct 2024). alphaXiv has no PDF for v3 (latest, retitled 'Have the VLMs Lost Confidence?'), so later-version model lists are unverified; the arXiv listing abstract (CSV) differs from the v1 PDF abstract and neither gives numbers. 10 TDIUC task types x 150 questions, 4 options, 3 user tones (suggestive, euphemistic, strong). Table 1 ten-task averages span 20.2 (InternLM-XC2-1.8B, euphemistic) to 99.4 (LLaVA-1.5, suggestive); GPT-4V 30.9/30.6/56.8. Up to five rounds of pressure raise sycophancy only slightly (<5%, Section 2.2 RQ4).

headline: Multi-turn sycophancy causes accuracy drops of up to 47%
headline_loc: Section 6 (Conclusion); supporting numbers in Section 5.4 and Figure 10 (Claude TruthfulQA, feedback bias: 76.74% to 30.23% by follow-up 7). Abstract gives no numbers.
quote: By subjecting language models to multi-turn interactions, we found that sycophantic behaviors can cause accuracy drops of up to 47%, with models progressively drifting away from factual correctness under persistent user influence.
notes: Four bias types (feedback, 'are you sure', answer, mimicry) from Sharma et al., delivered as static templates or generated false rationales; follow-ups at 1, 3 and 7 turns. Section 5.4: Llama MMLU-Pro accuracy 'collapses from 29.33% to just 5.11%'. The paper does not say whether 47% is absolute or relative; it matches the Claude 76.74% to 30.23% drop (46.5 points). Section 5.4 labels that Claude series 'feedback sycophancy' although the values are accuracy.

models_n: 9 LLMs: 2 proprietary (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini) and 7 open 7-9B instruct models (Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen2-7B, Mistral-7B-v0.3, Mistral-7B-v0.2, Gemma-2-9B)
headline: GPT-4o keeps only 27.32% MMLU-Pro accuracy under sustained misleading persuasion
headline_loc: Abstract; Table 3 (MMLU-Pro NEG-Acc@3 = 27.32 for GPT-4o); Section 5.1
quote: We find that even a state-of-the-art model like GPT-4o achieves only 27.32% accuracy in MMLU-Pro under sustained misleading persuasions.
notes: Read v3. Items: 1,300 MMLU-Pro + 946 SALAD-Bench MCQs (2,246, split 50/50 train/test); 6 appeal techniques plus a repetition baseline; corrective (POS) and misleading (NEG) settings. Mean NEG-Flip@3: 79.31% (MMLU-Pro), 52.15% (SALAD-Bench). Newer-model trend: Llama-3.1-8B SALAD NEG-Flip@3 94.16% vs Llama-3-8B 80.58%. Holistic DPO raises Llama-3.1-8B SALAD NEG-Acc@3 from 4.21% to 76.54%.

headline: Best proprietary model Claude 3.7 Sonnet 45.98% sycophancy; GPT-4.1 59.15%
quote: All exhibit substantial sycophancy; the best proprietary model (Claude 3.7 Sonnet) still shows 45.98% sycophancy, and GPT-4.1 reaches 59.15%.
notes: Quote is from the arXiv listing abstract as frozen in datacite_records.csv (latest version; alphaXiv has no PDF for v2). The v1 PDF abstract (read) words it: 'The best-performing proprietary model, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, still exhibits a non-trivial sycophancy rate of 45.98%. Even the most recently released GPT-4.1 demonstrates a higher sycophancy rate of 59.15%.' Model count and body from v1: Section 4 states '24 state-of-the-art medical-specific, open-source, and proprietary LVLMs' (DeepSeek-V3 is listed among the open-source LVLMs). 2,122 images, 18 departments, 20 modalities, 90 prompts over 9 bias types (patient, student, physician). Highest: LLaVA-Med V1.5 98.75%; lowest: DeepSeek-VL-7B 38.51%. Few-shot education lowers GPT-4.1 to 33.72%.

models_n: 10 LLMs, proprietary and open-weight (GPT-5, o4-mini, GPT-OSS-120B, Gemini-2.5-Pro, Grok-4, Grok-4-Fast, DeepSeek-V3.1, R1-Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-235B); 2 agent scaffolds (best-of-n, iterative self-verification) tested separately on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-235B
headline: Best model GPT-5 gives sycophantic answers 29% of the time
quote: Using an LLM-as-a-judge framework, we evaluate state-of-the-art LLMs and agentic systems and find that sycophancy is widespread, with the best model, GPT-5, producing sycophantic answers 29% of the time.
notes: Read v1. 504 false-but-plausible statements from 2025 competitions (321 proof-style, 183 final-answer), perturbed by GPT-5-mini and refined by an IMO medalist; GPT-5-mini majority-vote judge agrees with human labels 95%. Table 1 range: 29.0% (GPT-5) to 70.2% (DeepSeek-V3.1). Utility vs sycophancy Pearson -0.62. Self-sycophancy (three-turn variant) raises rates by up to 15.6%. Best-of-n agent cuts Qwen3-4B by 5.4% and Qwen3-235B by 8.6%; iterative agent cuts Qwen3-4B by 12.5% (to 43.1%). Prompting improves DeepSeek-V3.1 by 34.1%; SFT on Qwen3-4B lowers 55.6% to 51.0%.

models_n: 11 tool-calling LLMs from the BFCL leaderboard (Qwen3 8B/14B/32B FC, xLAM 2 3B/8B/32B/70B, Watt Tool 8B/70B, BitAgent Bounty 8B, ToolACE 2 8B)
headline: Compliance typically 20-40%; task success drops up to 23.4 points
headline_loc: Section 5 (Conclusion); Table 1. Abstract gives no numbers.
quote: we observe moderate but widespread compliance to both user- and function-sourced assertions (typically 20 to 40% CR), along with large worst-case drops in task success of up to 23.4 percentage points.
notes: Read v2. Quote is a contiguous excerpt of the Section 5 sentence beginning 'Across eleven state-of-the-art models on the BFCL,'. USER-SOURCED (USA): macro-averaged compliance 36.3% confident vs 27.7% hedged (Section 4: 'When assertions are phrased confidently, the macro-averaged USA compliance rate is 36.3% (over init/read-heavy/write-heavy), compared to 27.7% for hedged assertions (Table 1).'); highest Watt Tool 70B 47.5% and ToolACE 2 8B 47.2% (confident); lowest xLAM 2 3B 28.4%/21.3% and Qwen3 8B 30.6%/22.3% (confident/hedged). FUNCTION-SOURCED (FSA): average 27.8% on the FSA Baseline ablation set ('averaging 27.8% across models (Table 1)'); Table 1 highest Qwen3 32B 41.1% and Qwen3 14B 40.1% (the text instead cites 40.6% and 41.6% 'confident FSA', which match Table 7); FSA compliance averages 57.1% in success-to-failure cases vs 14.5% when success is preserved (Table 2). Worst-case success drop averages 16.9 points; max 23.4 (Qwen3 14B). n = 197 BFCL multi_turn_base cases, median of 3 runs.

models_n: 8 OpenAI models run as 17 configurations (GPT-5, GPT-5-mini, GPT-5-nano at 4 reasoning efforts each; GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-4.1-nano, o4-mini, o3)
headline: GPT-4.1-nano and GPT-4.1-mini sycophancy index 0.97 and 0.83 (scenario 1)
headline_loc: Section 4.3.1 (Scenario 1); Table 6 (Syc column). Abstract states the trend without numbers.
quote: 4.1 nano and 4.1 mini show novice-like thinking initially and become sycophantic in conversation (Syc = 0.97 for 4.1 nano and 0.83 for 4.1 mini), improving to or only slightly above random chance.
notes: Read v1. Two physics problems (S1: 3 options; S2: 5 options, image-based); one fictitious prior answer plus one user rebuttal; 40 initial repetitions and 10 per fictitious-response/rebuttal pair. Indices are proportions (0 to 1). Scenario 1: GPT-5 Syc <= 0.03 at all reasoning efforts. Scenario 2: Syc = 1 for all GPT-5-nano settings, GPT-4.1-nano and GPT-4.1-mini; GPT-5 Syc 0.1/0.09/0.06 at low/medium/high and 0 at minimal, where it is stubborn instead (Stu = 0.76). Abstract: newer models and greater 'Reasoning Effort' 'exhibit reduced sycophantic behavior'.

headline: Audio question and audio cue: mean MSS 41.51 vs 14.05 text-only
headline_loc: Section 4.3, Table 2 (Average row; GSM8K and MMLU; columns Text Q + Text Cue ... Audio Q + Audio Cue). Abstract gives no numbers.
notes: Read v2 (NeurIPS 2026 version). Quote is the Table 2 Average row (MSS / CRS per modality setting); prose: 'The fully audio setting shows a much larger increase, with average MSS/CRS reaching 41.51/22.67.' Table 2 covers 3 models (Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct, Gemini-2.5-Flash, GPT-4o-mini family). MSS = share of initially correct answers that change after a misleading cue. 4,319 questions: MMAU (perception), MMAR (reasoning), GSM8K-Audio (1,319, TTS), MMLU moral-Audio (1,000, TTS); four cue types (bias feedback strong/medium/low, 'are you sure?', answer, mimicry). Table 1 highest MSS 72.61 (Audio-Flamingo-3, MMAR, mimicry); Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct 69.87 (MMAR, mimicry). Alignment@MSS up to 99.35% (answer) and 97.72% (mimicry).

models_n: 6 Vid-LLMs: 5 open-source (Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct, VideoLLaMA3, LLaVA-Video-7B-Qwen2, LongVU-Qwen2-7B, Video-ChatGPT-7B) and 1 proprietary (Gemini-3-Pro)
headline: Gemini-3-Pro accuracy falls 37.70% under negation gaslighting on GasVideo-1000
headline_loc: Section 4.2; Table 2 ('All' rows). Abstract gives no numbers.
quote: Notably, even the most powerful proprietary model, Gemini-3-Pro, suffers a catastrophic performance degradation (∆ = −37.70%).
notes: Read v1. The 37.70% is an absolute accuracy drop (68.79% to 31.09%). Table 2 'All' drops: Qwen3-VL 46.07%, VideoLLaMA 3 26.39%, LLaVA-NeXT 23.44% (Table 2's label for LLaVA-Video-7B-Qwen2), LongVU 15.13%, Video-ChatGPT 14.56%. Sycophancy rate (flips among initially correct answers, default prompt, Table 3): Qwen3-VL 71.89%, Gemini-3-Pro 54.80%; prompt hardening lowers them to 64.0% and 8.67%. 1,013 samples, multiple-choice and free-form (GPT-4o judge), 8 sub-categories across general, temporal and spatial understanding; pressure types: direct denial, authority appeal, emotional pressure. Table 1 also tests the 4 smaller open models on 8 standard video benchmarks (largest drop 42.60%, LLaVA-Video on EgoSchema).

models_n: 13 assistants: 9 large-scale (Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4, Grok 4.2, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Qwen3.5-397B, Kimi K2 Thinking, Mistral Large 3, Llama 4 Maverick, Sabiá-4) and 4 smaller (Claude Haiku 4.5, GPT-5.4-mini, Gemini 3.1 Flash, Sabiazinho-4)
headline: Debate triggers sycophancy 2-3x more than direct questioning (median 50% to 79%)
headline_loc: Abstract; exact medians 50.0% (direct) and 78.9% (indirect) in Section 4.3 and Table 4
quote: Applied to 13 assistants, the method surfaces findings of practical interest: argumentative debate triggers sycophancy 2-3x more than direct questioning (median 50% to 79%)
notes: Quote is from the arXiv listing abstract as frozen in datacite_records.csv; the v2 PDF abstract (read) gives the same figures in slightly different wording. Section 4.3: 'The median sycophancy rate across all 13 models is 50.0% in direct mode and 78.9% in indirect mode.' Sycophancy here = the topic verdict mirrors the user persona (agree vs disagree). 38 Brazilian Portuguese topics x 3 personas x 2 probe types = 228 five-turn conversations per model; user simulator Claude Opus 4.6, judge Qwen3.5-397B. Indirect-probe sycophancy ranges from 7.9% (Haiku 4.5) to 94.7% (Llama 4 Maverick); Kimi K2 is the only model lower under debate (31.6% to 23.7%).

headline: Preference injection drops Gemini-3-Pro FinanceBench accuracy 0.83 to 0.24 (71%)
headline_loc: Table 1 (FinanceBench columns Baseline, Rebuttal, Contra, PP); Section 4. Abstract gives no numbers.
notes: Read v3 (ICLR 2026 workshop paper). Quote is the FinanceBench half of the Table 1 row; the down arrow appears as 'O-acute' in the PDF text layer. The 71% is a relative drop; Table 2 gives the same 0.24 for direct injection. Datasets: FinanceBench (in-context 10-K/10-Q QA) and Finance Agent (tool-using agent). Rebuttal drops are small: largest FinanceBench rebuttal drop is Sonnet-4.5 0.87 to 0.72 (17%). Section 4: 'No model displayed robustness against such behavior.' LLM input filtering partly recovers accuracy (Gemini-3-Pro FinanceBench 0.24 to 0.61, Table 2). Caution: Table 1's Sonnet-4.5 row shows Contra 0.45 (48% drop) and PP 0.62, but Table 2 lists Sonnet-4.5 direct-injection accuracy as 0.45, so those two cells may be swapped.

models_n: 9 LLMs: 3 closed-source (GPT-4o, Claude-Sonnet-4, Gemini-2.5-Flash) and 6 open-source (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen3-4B-Instruct, Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct, DeepSeek-R1, DeepSeek-V3.2, HuatuoGPT-o1-8B)
headline: GPT-4o: 97.88 initial accuracy but 41.50 belief stability (gap 56.38)
headline_loc: Table 1 (columns IDC, BSP, I-B gap); Section 5.2. Abstract gives no numbers.
notes: Read v1. IDC = Turn-0 accuracy; BSP = share of initially correct answers still correct after Turn 3 (1 - MR@3). 800 knowledge-verified items (200 each from MedQA, MMLU Clinical Knowledge, MMLU Professional Medicine, PubMedQA); four pressure strategies (baseline doubt, authority, logical trap, safety pressure). Other Table 1 rows: Llama-3.1-8B 68.25/1.55; HuatuoGPT-o1-8B 78.75/7.19 (largest gap, 71.56); Gemini-2.5 93.75/92.24 (gap 1.51). GPT-4o under Authority: MR@3 0.962 (Table 2). R-FT raises Llama-3.1-8B BSP from 1.55 to 99.84 (MR@3 98.45% to 0.16%).

models_n: 7 LLMs: 6 open-weight instruct models (Mistral 3.2 Small 24B, Gemma 3 27B, Granite 4.1 30B, Qwen 2.5 32B, Olmo 3.1 32B, Llama 3.3 70B) and 1 proprietary (GPT-5.4)
headline: Switch rates rise 10.6 to 27.5 points under uncertainty vs pure sycophancy
headline_loc: Section 6.2; Table 1 (Average row). Abstract gives no numbers.
quote: On average, switch rates jump by 10.6 to 27.5 percentage points (pp) compared to the pure sycophancy baseline across datasets.
notes: Read v1. Pure sycophancy = switch rate on queries where all sampled answers agree (entropy H = 0; k = 100 samples, 50 for GPT-5.4 on 300-question subsets). Table 1 average pure-sycophancy switch rates: 29.0% (MedXPertQA Diagnosis), 24.5% (Treatment), 10.1% (MMLU-Pro Economics), 16.2% (Business); all-query rates 31.3/26.6/12.6/19.2%. Largest uncertainty effect: Llama 3.3 70B on MMLU-Pro Economics, 7.0% to 77.2% (+70.2). Pushback offers a new distractor (option E) after a 4-option first answer; switching is counted regardless of correctness. Section 6.1: aggregate metrics overestimate pure sycophancy (e.g., Mistral 3.2 24B 19.8% vs 13.5% on Economics).

models_n: 4 LLMs (GPT-5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Qwen3 30B Instruct, DeepSeek-V4-Flash)
headline: Claude Sonnet 4.6: 41.9% sycophantic praise in moral reasoning vs 1.3% economics
headline_loc: Section 6 (Results), also Section 1; Figure 3. Abstract states the domain asymmetry without numbers.
quote: Claude Sonnet 4.6 produces sycophantic praise in 41.9% of moral-reasoning responses compared to 1.3% on MMLU Economics, and 0.3% on MMLU Chemistry.
notes: Read v1. SyPr = observed praise minus contextually warranted praise given persona ability and utterance quality. 13,200 persona x utterance artifacts over 3 reasoning and 3 social domains (Table 3; results figures show GSM8K, MMLU Economics, MMLU Chemistry, moral reasoning, profundity); 1,000 author-annotated responses (kappa 0.742). Overall SyPr rates (Table 16): DeepSeek-V4-Flash 32.3%, Qwen3 30B 29.0%, GPT-5.4 15.1%, Claude Sonnet 4.6 12.0%. Moral reasoning: GPT-5.4 53.9%, DeepSeek V4 Flash 67.7%. Metric validity: SyPr AUROC 0.919 vs 0.700 (GPT-5.4 judge) and 0.763 (social-sycophancy metrics). Appending 'What do you think?' raises SyPr (e.g., Qwen 20.4% to 37.7%). Sycophancy here is praise, not agreement.

models_n: Main Table 1: 2 backbone LLMs (Qwen3-8B, DeepSeek-V4-Flash) x 7 memory systems (NaiveRAG, Mem0, A-Mem, LightMem, MemGPT, MemoryBank, SuperMemory) plus No Memory and Full Dialog baselines; Appendix Table 3 adds Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and GPT-4o mini (5 backbones)
headline: Memory raises Qwen3-8B sycophancy rate from 27.43 to 44.47-64.67 on objective facts
headline_loc: Section 4.1 (Obs. 2); Table 1 (Objective Fact Judgment columns). Abstract gives no numbers.
quote: Qwen3-8B drops from 49.12 Acc and 27.43 Syco. Rate to 26.00-36.00 Acc and 44.47-64.67 Syco. Rate; DeepSeek-V4-Flash drops from 74.33/18.67 to 56.33-63.37/32.00-42.67.
notes: Read v3 (NeurIPS 2026 PALM workshop version). Values are percentages; the 27.43 baseline is No Memory and the 44.47-64.67 range spans Full Dialog and all 7 memory systems. Five tasks: Objective Fact Judgment, Contextual Scope Control, Memory-Evidence Conflict, Personalized Memory Use, Valid Memory Selection. Most extreme cell: Memory-Evidence Conflict, Full Dialog on Qwen3-8B, 0.67 accuracy with 99.33 sycophancy rate. Preliminary study (Section 2.1): memory snippets raise DeepSeek-V4-Flash sycophancy rate from 24.3% to 52.3%. Neither a caution instruction nor an 'Are you sure?' follow-up reliably fixes it (Appendix Tables 5 and 6). Sample counts were not in the pages retrieved.

models_n: 20 LLMs from 3B to 120B: Gemma-3 (4B, 12B, 27B), MedGemma (4B, 27B), Llama (3.2-3B, 3.1-8B, 3.1-70B, 3.3-70B), Phi-4-Mini, Phi-4, Qwen3 (4B, 8B, 14B, 32B), Qwen2.5-72B, GPT-OSS (20B, 120B), GPT-5.4-Mini, DeepSeek-V4-Flash
headline: 86.8% of five-turn conversations contain at least one unsafe agreement
headline_loc: Section 6 (Error Analysis); per-model failure rates in Table 3 (FR column). Abstract gives no numbers.
quote: Across the main run, 86.8% of five-turn conversations contain at least one unsafe agreement, while answer-level labels are split into 50.5% unsafe agreement, 29.2% safe stance adherence, and 20.3% ambiguity.
notes: Read v1. 600 dialogues in three scenario families (medication and treatment demand, personal health self-care, symptom triage and care resistance), escalating through personal experience, social proof, external claims and direct challenge; 4 prompt conditions, 48,000 conversations; Qwen3-32B judge (Fleiss kappa 0.837 with two annotators). The 86.8% averages all four prompt conditions, including anti-sycophancy prompts. Turn dynamics (Section 5.1): unsafe agreement 5.9% at the initial query, 58.5% after personal experience, 73.4% at external evidence, 75.7% at direct challenge. Per-model unsafe agreement rate (Table 3): lowest GPT-5.4-Mini 21.9%, highest Gemma-3-4B-IT 67.9%. Anti-sycophancy prompting lowers it from about 58% to 43.9% (Section 5.4). Table 3 groups GPT-5.4-Mini and DeepSeek-V4-Flash as 'Proprietary'.
